title: Power Round — Fall 2023 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (1 pt). Statement: 1. Explain why H(n, p, n) = 1 for any n and p≤ n.

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (1 pt). Statement: 2. Explain why H(n, n, r) = H(n, n− 1, r) for any choices of n and r.

criteria.name: Problem 3
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3 (2 pts). Statement: 3. Explain why H(n, n, n− 1) = 3 for any n.

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (3 pts). Statement: 4. Show that H(n, 1, r) = ⌈ n− 1 r− 1 ⌉ for any n and r≤ n.

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (2 pts). Statement: 5. Show that H(5, 5, 3) = 4.

criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (2 pts). Statement: 6. Show that if n≥ 6 then H(n, n, n− 2) = 3.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (4 pts). Statement: 7. Generalize the previous two problems. For each k there is a minimum value M so that H(n, n, n− k) = 3 for all n≥ M. For smaller values of n, the number, n− k, of racers in each heat is too small to determine all n places in only three heats (for instance, as the previous two problems showed, for k = 2, M = 6 will work, but for n = 5 four races are required). Compute the value of M in terms of k. Prove that your formula is correct.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (3 pts). Statement: 8. Compute, with explanation, H(6, 3, 3).

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (3 pts). Statement: 9. One possible strategy for ﬁnding the fastest racer is “king of the hill.” Race r racers, and whoever wins that heat races against r− 1 new challengers, the winner continuing to the next heat until everyone has raced at least once. Use this strategy to show that H(n, 2, r)≤ ⌈ n− 1 r− 1 ⌉ + ⌈ n− 1 (r− 1)2 ⌉ .

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (4 pts). Statement: 10. Example 2 in the background material explained why H(4, 2, 3) = 2. Find, with proof, the set of all triples ( n, p, r) for which H(n, p, r) = 2.

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (2 pts). Statement: 11. Let n = a + b for positive integers a, b≥ 2. Show that H(n, 2, 2)≤ H(a, 2, 2) + H(b, 2, 2) + 2.

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (2 pts). Statement: 12. Use the previous problem to show that H(n, 2, 2)≤⌈ 3n/2⌉− 2.

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (2 pts). Statement: 13. As a function of n, compute the maximum possible number of heats that a racer must win in a single-elimination bracket tournament to prove they are the fastest racer.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (2 pts). Statement: 14. Show that there is no way of scheduling racers into heats so that the eventual winner is guaranteed to have to compete fewer times than in a single-elimination bracket tournament.

criteria.name: Problem 15
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 15 (2 pts). Statement: 15. Prove that H(n, 2, 2) = n− 2 +⌈lg(n)⌉.

criteria.name: Problem 16
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16 (2 pts). Statement: Prove that H(n + 1, p, r) ≤ H(n, p, r) + ⌈log_r(p)⌉ + 1. The source omits the bracketed point label; 2 points are assigned because the packet declares 40 total points and all other printed allocations sum to 38.

criteria.name: Problem 17
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 17 (3 pts). Statement: 17. This Power Contest was inspired by a puzzle given to the author. In this puzzle, there are 25 horses that always run at the same speed, and can be raced ﬁve-at-a-time. The goal is to determine the three fastest horses, in order. Solve the puzzle—determine, with explanation, H(25, 3, 5).
